name: DigitalisFhirHub
title: Digitalis fhir-hub Implementation Guide
description: FHIR R4 conformance artifacts for the Digitalis FHIR interface: two contracts on two FHIR bases — Prescriptor, the prescribing sessions of $formulary-session, $createrx-session and $session-result, and Surveillance, whose $check-medication-request weighs proposed prescriptions against a patient's dossier and whose $check-medication-statement weighs the dossier itself, both answering with the signals that fire.

resource.name: $check-medication-request example
resource.description: One proposed prescription weighed against a patient's current medication, allergy, contra-indication and lab result.

resource.name: $check-medication-request example, the reference case
resource.description: The FHIR form of the request Digitalis documents as example-1-req.xml: metformine proposed for a pregnant patient with an eGFR of 35 who already takes ibuprofen and omeprazol. It is the payload behind the three beslisregel signals in that document's response, and it also raises the classic allergy and dose-control signals.

resource.name: $check-medication-request input
resource.description: The body of POST /fhir/surveillance/$check-medication-request: the patient's context plus the prescriptions to check against it. A conformant request is weighed by the G-Standaard's medisch-farmaceutische beslisregels and by the classic allergy, age, duplicate-medication and dose checks, and the signals come back as a Bundle of DetectedIssue.

resource.name: $check-medication-statement example
resource.description: A patient's current medication checked against itself and their context: two drugs, an allergy and an eGFR of 35, with no prescription proposed. Note that there is no prescription parameter — this profile does not define one.

resource.name: $check-medication-statement input
resource.description: The body of POST /fhir/surveillance/$check-medication-statement: a patient's context and the medication they are already taking, with every entry under test rather than serving as the background to a proposal. The signals come back as a Bundle of DetectedIssue, exactly as for $check-medication-request.

resource.name: $createrx-session input
resource.description: The body of POST /fhir/$createrx-session. Prescribing without a formulary lookup, optionally starting from a prescription the host already holds.

resource.name: $createrx-session request
resource.description: A CreateRx session opened on a prescription the host already holds. No reason for encounter: CreateRx prescribes without a formulary lookup.

resource.name: $formulary-session input
resource.description: The body of POST /fhir/$formulary-session. Opens a formulary session: the care provider picks a treatment for a stated reason for encounter.

resource.name: $formulary-session request
resource.description: A formulary session with one allergy, one contra-indication, one current drug and one lab result.

resource.name: $session-result output
resource.description: The finished session: zero or more prescriptions and zero or more advice texts. An empty Bundle is a valid answer — the care provider may have prescribed nothing.

resource.name: $session-result response
resource.description: One prescription, one prose advice and one pointer to patient information.

resource.name: Administrative gender accepted by Prescriptor
resource.description: Prescriptor's PatientGender has three values — M, F and X — so FHIR's 'other' has no upstream equivalent.

resource.name: Allergy causative agent (SSK, SNK, OGGrp)
resource.description: Causative agents fhir-hub routes to Prescriptor. Which member carries which subsystem is set by prescriptor-api's OpenSessionRequestBuilder.getAllergies.

resource.name: Coded directions (NHG Tabel 25)
resource.description: The NHG Tabel 25 coded usage instruction, verbatim, e.g. '3-4D1S; gedurende max. 1 maand'.

resource.name: Contra-indication (CICode or ICPC-1 NL)
resource.description: Contra-indications fhir-hub routes to Prescriptor, as either a G-Standaard CICode or an ICPC-1 NL code.

resource.name: fhir-hub advice
resource.description: One advice text produced by the session, either prose or a pointer to patient information.

resource.name: fhir-hub AllergyIntolerance
resource.description: A known hypersensitivity, coded in a G-Standaard subsystem Prescriptor routes.

resource.name: fhir-hub Condition
resource.description: A contra-indication, coded as a G-Standaard CICode or an ICPC-1 NL code.

resource.name: fhir-hub laboratory Observation
resource.description: A single laboratory determination or body measurement, coded in LOINC, from the closed list of determinations medication surveillance reads.

resource.name: fhir-hub MedicationStatement
resource.description: One entry of the patient's current medication, for medication surveillance.

resource.name: fhir-hub Patient
resource.description: The demographics a session needs. Only gender and birthDate are read; anything else you send is ignored and never forwarded to Prescriptor or stored.

resource.name: fhir-hub prescription
resource.description: One prescription written in the session.

resource.name: fhir-hub prescription input
resource.description: A prescription the host already holds, handed to $createrx-session to open for editing. The mirror image of what $session-result returns, so a host can hand back a prescription it received earlier without reshaping it.

resource.name: G-Standaard bijzondere kenmerken (Opiumwet)
resource.description: The Opiumwet subset of G-Standaard bestand BST401T (thesaurus BST922T). No OID is registered for this table, so a Digitalis-local URI is used.

resource.name: ICPC-1 NL
resource.description: Reason for encounter. The code shape is additionally constrained by an invariant, because ICPC-1 NL is not expanded here.

resource.name: Laboratory determinations medication surveillance reads
resource.description: The LOINC codes accepted on Parameters.parameter:observation. These are the codes the G-Standaard itself attaches to its MFB parameters (BST684T rows with MFBEXSRT = 4, 'LOINC / Nederlandse Labcodeset'), so the rules engine can test what a host sends: eGFR, kalium, INR, sirolimus, natrium and lithium, plus weight and height for dose checking. One eGFR code only — Dutch laboratories report CKD-EPI, so the MDRD and cystatin C codes the G-Standaard also lists are not accepted here.

resource.name: Medication code (PRK or HPK)
resource.description: Product code levels accepted for current medication. Each entry carries its own level, so PRK and HPK may be mixed within one list.

resource.name: Medication surveillance finding
resource.description: One signal from Dutch medication surveillance: a medisch-farmaceutische beslisregel from the G-Standaard, or one of the classic allergy, age, duplicate-medication and dose checks. Route on identifier, show code.text, and read the full text from detail.

resource.name: Medication surveillance output
resource.description: What POST /fhir/surveillance/$check-medication-request and POST /fhir/surveillance/$check-medication-statement return: one DetectedIssue per signal, in the order the clinical-rules report listed them. An empty Bundle means the check ran and no rule fired — every way for the check not to happen is a 500 instead, never a 200 with no findings.

resource.name: Medication surveillance response
resource.description: Two signals from one report: a nierfunctie beslisregel firing red on a proposed metformine, and an allergy check that ran and matched nothing. Bundle.identifier is the report id to quote in a support question.

resource.name: Opiumwet classification
resource.description: Opiumwet classification of the prescribed product, as a G-Standaard bijzonder kenmerk.

resource.name: Opiumwet classification
resource.description: The Opiumwet codes from G-Standaard BST401T rubriek 72.

resource.name: Prescribed medication code (PRK, GPK, HPK or ATC)
resource.description: Codings that may appear on a MedicationRequest returned by $session-result. Exactly one of PRK, GPK and HPK is present — the level the prescription was written at — with an ATC beside it when the upstream supplies one.

resource.name: Prescription input medication code (PRK, HPK or ATC)
resource.description: Codings accepted on the prescription handed to $createrx-session. An ATC may accompany the product code but cannot stand alone.

resource.name: Session input (shared base)
resource.description: Everything the two session operations have in common. Use FhirHubFormularySessionInput or FhirHubCreateRxSessionInput rather than this directly.

resource.name: Session output
resource.description: What both session operations return: the launch URL and the session id the host later polls with.

resource.name: Session response
resource.description: What both session operations return.
